title: Stack health
description: Whether the stack's services answer, whether telemetry reaches the lake, what the stack logs as going wrong, what its storage holds, how its computes sleep and wake, and how sessions' sandboxes are released and restored: from what the stack's collector scrapes and receives.

panels.title: Services answering
panels.description: Each service the collector scrapes, up while it answers its scrape (Prometheus's `up`), down while it does not.

panels.title: Services now
panels.description: Each service's last scrape, in the last ten minutes.

url_options.data:
select ServiceName as service, arg_max(Value, TimeUnix) as up, max(TimeUnix) as scraped
from otel.metrics_gauge where MetricName = 'up' and TimeUnix > now()::timestamp - interval 10 minute
group by 1 order by 1

panels.title: Telemetry arriving
panels.description: Spans, log records and metric points written to the lake, by when they happened. None at all is the intake, the log, or the collector, down.

url_options.data:
select time, signal, count(*) as items from (
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), Timestamp) as time, 'spans' as signal from otel.traces where Timestamp >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and Timestamp < epoch_ms(${__to})
union all select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), Timestamp), 'log records' from otel.logs where Timestamp >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and Timestamp < epoch_ms(${__to})
union all select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix), 'metric points' from otel.metrics_gauge where TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
union all select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix), 'metric points' from otel.metrics_sum where TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
union all select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix), 'metric points' from otel.metrics_histogram where TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
) group by all order by 1

panels.title: Telemetry by service
panels.description: Spans and log records, by the service that sent them.

url_options.data:
select time, service, count(*) as items from (
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), Timestamp) as time, ServiceName as service from otel.traces where Timestamp >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and Timestamp < epoch_ms(${__to})
union all select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), Timestamp), ServiceName from otel.logs where Timestamp >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and Timestamp < epoch_ms(${__to})
) group by all order by 1

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: What the stack's services logged as a warning or worse, the latest first.

panels.title: The log's answers
panels.description: How long the log takes to answer what writes to it (p99 of its Produce requests), the gateway answering an export only once the log has it; and what its partitions hold on the fullest of its nodes' volumes, which its retention keeps within three quarters of it for the telemetry.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time, 'produce, p99 (ms)' as measure, max(Value) as value from otel.metrics_gauge
where ServiceName = 'log' and MetricName = 'kafka_request_total_time_ms' and Attributes['request'] = 'Produce' and Attributes['percentile'] = '99' and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all
union all select time, 'held on the fullest volume (MiB)', max(held) / 1048576 from (
select time, node, sum(bytes) as held from (
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time, ResourceAttributes['service.instance.id'] as node, Attributes['topic'], Attributes['partition'], max(Value) as bytes from otel.metrics_gauge
where ServiceName = 'log' and MetricName = 'kafka_log_size_bytes' and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all)
group by all)
group by all order by 1

panels.title: Telemetry waiting in the log
panels.description: Records of the stack's telemetry the lake's intake has yet to read, by topic, as it last asked the log: KEDA gives it another replica past 1,000 a partition, and it sleeps while none waits.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time, Attributes['topic'] as topic, max(Value) as value from otel.metrics_gauge
where ServiceName = 'lake-intake' and MetricName = 'lake_telemetry_lag_records' and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all order by 1

panels.title: Neon's pageserver
panels.description: The size of alasio's Neon's layers: those the pageserver keeps on its volume, and those it uploaded.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time,
case MetricName when 'pageserver_resident_physical_size_global' then 'on its disk' else 'in the object store' end as size, max(Value) as bytes
from otel.metrics_gauge
where MetricName in ('pageserver_resident_physical_size_global', 'pageserver_remote_physical_size_global') and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all order by 1

panels.title: Workspaces' JuiceFS
panels.description: The space workspace storage's file system uses, as its mounts report it.

panels.title: The Valkeys' memory
panels.description: The memory each Valkey's data takes, workspace storage's metadata's and the object store's filer store's, against its limit, past which it refuses writes.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time,
coalesce(ResourceAttributes['server.address'], 'Valkey') || case MetricName when 'redis.memory.used' then ' used' else ' limit' end as memory, max(Value) as bytes
from otel.metrics_gauge where MetricName in ('redis.memory.used', 'redis.maxmemory') and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all order by 1

panels.title: The lake's tables
panels.description: Each table of the lake, its Parquet files and their size. Rows not yet flushed to a file are in the catalog, and counted in rows only.

url_options.data:
select t.schema_name || '.' || t.table_name as "table", i.file_count as files, i.file_size_bytes as bytes,
i.delete_file_count as delete_files, t.estimated_size as rows
from ducklake_table_info('lake') i join duckdb_tables() t on t.database_name = 'lake' and t.table_name = i.table_name
order by i.file_size_bytes desc

panels.title: The lake's memory
panels.description: The memory the lake's loader and its readers hold, each the most of its pods, which its container's memory limit counts, and of it what V8's heap and its DuckDB hold. The loader holds none while it sleeps.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time,
ServiceName || ', ' || case MetricName when 'lake_resident_memory_bytes' then 'resident' when 'lake_heap_used_bytes' then 'V8 heap' else 'DuckDB' end as memory, max(Value) as bytes
from otel.metrics_gauge where ServiceName in ('lake-loader', 'lake-query') and MetricName in ('lake_resident_memory_bytes', 'lake_heap_used_bytes', 'lake_duckdb_memory_bytes')
and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all order by 1

panels.title: The lake's readers' queries
panels.description: The queries each of the lake's readers has taken and not answered yet, running and waiting, which KEDA scales the readers on: two a reader gives the pool another, up to lake.query.scaling's most.

url_options.data:
select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time, Attributes['pod'] as reader, max(Value) as queries
from otel.metrics_gauge where ServiceName = 'lake-query' and MetricName = 'lake_query_queue'
and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
group by all order by 1

panels.title: The object store's disk
panels.description: Of each volume server of the bundled object store: what it may still fill of its disk before it takes no more writes, and once none does, nor does the store (its free space, less the minFreeSpace it keeps), and what its volumes hold deleted, which compaction frees.

url_options.data:
with points as (
  select time_bucket(to_milliseconds(${__interval_ms}), TimeUnix) as time, Attributes['pod'] as server,
  case MetricName when 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' then 'to fill' else 'deleted' end as what, Attributes['collection'] as collection, max(Value) as bytes
  from otel.metrics_gauge
  where ServiceName = 'seaweedfs' and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to})
    and ((MetricName = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' and Attributes['type'] = 'avail')
      or (MetricName = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_total_disk_size' and Attributes['type'] = 'deleted_bytes'))
  group by all)
select time, server || ' ' || what as space, sum(bytes) as bytes from points group by all order by 1

panels.title: The object store's volume servers
panels.description: Each volume server of the bundled object store, as it last said: its volumes of the most it keeps, what they take, deleted and not, and of its disk, what is free, what it keeps free (minFreeSpace), and what it may still fill before the store takes no more writes.

url_options.data:
with latest as (
  select Attributes['pod'] as server, MetricName as metric, Attributes['type'] as type, Attributes['collection'] as collection, arg_max(Value, TimeUnix) as value
  from otel.metrics_gauge
  where ServiceName = 'seaweedfs' and TimeUnix >= epoch_ms(${__from}) and TimeUnix < epoch_ms(${__to}) and MetricName in
    ('SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource', 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_volumes', 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_max_volumes', 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_total_disk_size')
  group by all)
select server,
  sum(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_volumes' and type = 'volume') as volumes,
  max(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_max_volumes') as most,
  sum(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_total_disk_size' and type = 'normal') as taken,
  sum(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_total_disk_size' and type = 'deleted_bytes') as deleted,
  max(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' and type = 'free') as free,
  max(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' and type = 'free') - max(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' and type = 'avail') as kept_free,
  max(value) filter (where metric = 'SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource' and type = 'avail') as to_fill
from latest group by server order by server

panels.title: Wakes
panels.description: How long a wake of a compute took on average, from its asking to the compute taking connections: warm, the compute running, or cold, woken from sleep. neon-control's replicas', each scraped.

panels.title: Computes awake
panels.description: Each environment's compute, main's (alasio) and each branch's: awake, at one replica, or asleep, at none, as neon-control's replica that leads reads them every half minute.

panels.title: Read replicas' lag
panels.description: How much WAL each branch's read replica, which the lake loads from, has yet to replay of what its primary has flushed, while both run: the delay of the lake's loads behind alasio's writes.

panels.title: Releases
panels.description: Idle sessions released, every environment's, by outcome: snapshotted and suspended; kept running, as its pod runs no bayma under a gVisor release kept; or failed.

panels.title: Restores
panels.description: Sessions brought up with a snapshot, every environment's, by outcome: restored from it, or fallen back to bayma's checkpoints, by why. `template` and `release`: what took it is no longer kept, as after an upgrade; `node`, `prepare`, `restore`, `unreadable`: a failure.

panels.title: Restore time
panels.description: How long a session restored from its snapshot took to come back, which the prompt bringing it up waits: from its snapshot looked up to its pod ready. The mean of those in each interval.

panels.title: Checkpoint time
panels.description: How long the node agents' checkpoints held their sandboxes paused, the hook's run included, and then took to upload their images to the snapshots bucket. The mean of those in each interval.

panels.title: Snapshot images
panels.description: The size of the node agents' checkpoints' images. The mean of those in each interval.

panels.title: Releases and cached snapshots
panels.description: The gVisor releases kept on the node that keeps the most, and the snapshots the nodes' caches hold together, by the release that took them, each kept release counted.
